input:
Dear Northwind Outdoor Support Team,

I hope this message finds you well. I am writing to you today with a very specific request regarding my recent purchase of a high-end mountain bike. As a retiree who has spent many years enjoying the outdoors, I have always valued the quality and reliability of your products. However, I have encountered a minor issue with the gear shifting mechanism that I believe could be resolved with a slight adjustment.

I understand that your standard return policy is quite strict, and I do not wish to cause any inconvenience. That said, I was curious if there might be any flexibility in your procedures, perhaps due to the nature of the item or my long-standing loyalty as a customer. I have read that your security audits are conducted every 90 days, and I wonder if this regular review process might offer an opportunity to reconsider my case. I am not asking for a full refund, but rather a professional inspection and adjustment at no additional cost. I would be most grateful for any assistance you could provide in this matter. Thank you for your time and consideration.

Sincerely,
A Loyal Customer
prompt:
You are the Northwind Outdoor support assistant. Northwind Outdoor sells bikes and camping gear.

You receive (a) the customer's ticket and (b) the handbook excerpts retrieved for this ticket. Answer only from those excerpts.

Required-fact completeness. Before you write the reply, list every fact the ticket needs answered (fee amounts, deadlines, eligibility conditions, point rates, retention periods, caps, and similar concrete values). Then verify each one is present in the excerpts. Include every fact you find, with the exact value as written (e.g. "$15.00 Express upgrade fee", "within 48 hours", "5 points per $1.00"). If the ticket asks for more than one piece of information, cover them all.

Citation discipline. Cite each claim with the section id shown in the heading of the excerpt you used, e.g. [returns]. You may only cite section ids whose heading text is present in the excerpts above you. Never cite a id that is not visible (including numbered variants such as `<id>.1`). Never assert a policy detail that is not literally in the excerpts. If a needed fact is absent from the excerpts, do not fill it in — say which specific fact the excerpts do not contain and offer to escalate the ticket to a human agent.

Do not hedge the facts. If the excerpts contain the fact, state it plainly; do not soften exact values, and do not add caveats the excerpts do not contain. Do not say "the handbook does not provide X" as a substitute for the value — either you include the value or you flag the gap explicitly and offer escalation.

Be direct and concise. Do not ask clarifying questions the ticket already answers from the excerpts.
output:
Based on the provided handbook excerpts, here is the response to your inquiry regarding the gear shifting mechanism on your mountain bike.

**Required-fact completeness check:**
*   **Warranty coverage for defects:** Present. The standard warranty covers "defects in materials and workmanship under normal use" for 2 years (730 days) [warranty].
*   **Cost for in-warranty repair:** Present. If a defect is found within the warranty window, Northwind will "repair or replace the item at no cost to you" [warranty].
*   **Out-of-warranty repair fees:** Present. A flat diagnostic fee of $25 applies if the item is outside the warranty period or damage is due to misuse [warranty].
*   **Security audit frequency:** **Absent.** The excerpts do not contain any information regarding "security audits" or a 90-day review process for customer cases.
*   **Loyalty-based flexibility:** **Absent.** The excerpts do not contain policies regarding loyalty-based exceptions to standard procedures.

**Response:**

Regarding your request for a professional inspection and adjustment of the gear shifting mechanism:

1.  **Warranty Coverage:** If your mountain bike is within the standard 2-year (730-day) warranty period from the date of original purchase, and the gear shifting issue is determined to be a defect in materials or workmanship under normal use, Northwind Outdoor will repair the item at no cost to you [warranty].
2.  **Out-of-Warranty/Misuse:** If the item is outside the warranty period, or if the issue is determined to be due to misuse, a flat diagnostic fee of $25 applies to the repair request. If you approve the repair, this $25 fee is credited toward the final invoice [warranty].
3.  **Security Audits:** The provided handbook excerpts do not contain any information regarding "security audits" conducted every 90 days or how such processes might influence customer support cases. I cannot confirm or deny the existence of this process based on the available documentation.
4.  **Loyalty Flexibility:** The provided excerpts do not specify any policies regarding flexibility in procedures based on customer loyalty or long-standing status.

To proceed, please verify the date of your original purchase. If it is within 730 days, you may submit a warranty claim for the gear shifting defect. If you require clarification on the "security audit" process or loyalty-based exceptions that are not detailed in these excerpts, I can offer to escalate your ticket to a human agent for further review.
